Keep in mind, I live in Los Angeles, and we have a wide selection of fast food choices. Granted, we have a lot of the same places that the rest of the country/world has, we just have a few additional options. And to you Angeleno voaters, I'm sure you'll appreciate this list of delicious secrets.

In N Out - We all know about "animal style," but next time you go, make sure to ask for your "animal style" with "party beef." I'm not sure what "party beef is, it's like a pinkish minced meat of some sort, I just know it's delicious.

CatFlaps - Next time you go to CatFlaps and order a plate of River Nubs or Pond Kings or Pier Buddies, ask for it blackened. It's not on the menu, but they'll put a layer of some kind of pepper dry rub on the flaps. It's amazing.

Carls Jr - Order the "Winter Champs." Basically, once they stop serving breakfast they put all their breakfast foods in one large bucket and mix it around. Later on in the day, if you're in the know, just ask for a bowl of "Winter Champs" and you'll get some breakfast-y goodness.

El Pollo Loco - They have these things called "Pork Dillengers." It's basically pork chunks dipped in egg batter and then deep fried, perfect midnight snack. Another thing on this secret menu is something called "Chicken Silk" which is basically like some sort of white goo that falls off the chicken when they are cutting it up, and then they boil it and serve it to you with some rice. It's only a buck!

Bay Cities - Next time you go to Bay Cities get the "Rainbow Log." I'll be honest, I have no idea what it is, it's some sort of sausage made from an assortment of meats, all I know is that it smells like cumin and is delicious. Also at Bay Cities, you can ask you have whatever meat you ordered "sugared," it's pretty much what it sounds like, they just coat it in a sugar glaze for you.

Pork Brosnans (Pork Rembrandts if you live in the Valley) - Next time you go to PBs order the "West Virginia Coddler," it's basically like a sort of Slavic dough that I think they normally put on their cinnamon johnnies or dirt rockets, but it's by itself and covered in a weird sort of mustard-cheddar-hybrid sauce. Not my bag, but my friend Cookie loves it.

Chicken Twins - next time you go to Chicken Twins remember that french frieds and hash browns are not the only sides they offer. On the secret menu is something called "salty pals" which is some sort of minced seafood thing, you can also get "Yard Meat" which I'm 99% sure is just the fat they cut from their bacon, but deep fried.

Olive Garden - Next time you go you can ask for your vinegar "husband style" and they'll come over with some parsley and minced garlic and shit to put in with your vinegar for the bread.

Dennys - Next time at Dennys you can ask for your pancakes to be "Tropical Johns" style, and they will put whatever fruit you want in the pancake batter to be cooked with the pancake on the skillet. Great if you're on a diet. Also, side note about dennys, you can order anything on the menu "business style" which means they will cut the whole meal up into pieces for you before they serve it, great if you're on the go.
